title: A CT-based deep-learning system stratifies postoperative pancreatic cancer prognosis
summary: A retrospective three-hospital study of 592 surgically treated pancreatic cancer patients evaluated a CT-based Swin Transformer classifier. Its disease-free-survival C-index was 0.807–0.844, versus 0.631–0.656 for clinicopathological predictors; their integrated model reached 0.836–0.871. A 41-patient molecular subset linked predicted risk with tumor microenvironment features. These are retrospective prognostic and molecular associations; treatment benefit and prospective clinical utility were not established.
ai_technology: Multi-planar Swin Transformer-assisted deep-learning classifier for CT radiomics
organization: Suzhou Ninth Hospital Affiliated to Soochow University; Suzhou Municipal Hospital, The Affiliated Suzhou Hospital of Nanjing Medical University; The First Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University; Renji Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Derivation: 308 patients; internal test: 78; separate external test: 206. A 41-patient derivation subset supported exploratory radiogenomic associations. Reported C-index ranges include derivation and test cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective selection, semiautomatic segmentation and treatment differences limit inference. Molecular patterns need larger independent validation; model-guided patient benefit was not tested.
evidence.ai_role: A multi-planar Swin Transformer learned CT prognostic features; IPSS-PDAC combined its risk output with clinicopathological factors.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher abstract, cohorts, CT preprocessing and Swin framework, radiogenomic methods, results/discussion/limitations, affiliations and online date; supplementary methods were not assessed.
